site.settings.consent.bannerText: This site uses only what it needs to work, unless you allow more. With your consent it also loads content from other services, such as videos, which may store data in your browser and use what they learn for their own purposes. You can change or withdraw your consent at any time, from the bottom of every page.
site.settings.consent.dialogIntroduction: Choose what the site may load and store beyond what it needs to work. Each category lists its services, who provides them, what they store and for how long. Your choice holds for 12 months. You can change or withdraw it at any time from the footer of every page.
site.settings.consent.noticeWithdrawn: Your consents have been withdrawn. The page will reload.
site.settings.consent.objectionText: We can't see who you are, we don't follow you from one visit to the next, and we don't profile you. All we do is count the visits: how many there are, which pages are read and for how long, from which country, in which language and with which browser, and when in the day. We do so on our legitimate interest in knowing this. If you disagree, you have the right to [object].
site.settings.consent.objectionObjected: You have objected to the counting, so your visits are not counted. [Undo your objection]
site.settings.consent.objectionAppeal: Do you really want us to stop counting your visits? We can't see who you are, and we don't follow you from one visit to the next. The figures help us understand what is valuable on the site and what we need to do better.
site.settings.consent.necessaryDescripti: What the site needs to work and to remember your choice. Always on.
site.settings.consent.functionalDescript: Content and features from other services, such as videos and charts, whose providers do not use what they learn for their own advertising or profiling.
site.settings.consent.statisticsDescript: Measuring how visitors use the site, so that it can be made better.
site.settings.consent.statisticsWithoutS: Measuring how visitors use the site, so that it can be made better. Each visit is counted from the first page, without storing anything in your browser or reading your device's properties. With your consent, the statistics also store an ID in your browser, so that a visitor who comes back is counted once.
site.settings.consent.marketingDescripti: Content and features from services whose providers may use what they learn about you for their own advertising or profiling.
site.settings.forms.confirmation: Thank you. Your message has been sent.

site.consent.declaration.column.name: Name
site.consent.declaration.departure.neces: {service} counts as necessary on this site, so it is always on, without your consent.
site.consent.declaration.departure.tagMa: The site's tag manager loads before you make a choice, and the tags it loads follow your choice.
site.consent.declaration.departure.stati: The site's statistics count each visit from the first page you see, before you make a choice, without storing anything in your browser and without reading your device's properties. They store in your browser only once you allow statistics.
A browser that sends Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track is not counted at all.
A browser that sends Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track is counted too, without storage until you allow statistics.

settings.search.label: Search and sharing
settings.search.description: What search engines and social networks show of the site's pages: the title tag, the meta description and the sharing card of each, made from its teaser where its type has one, and else from the templates below, its structured data type, and the publisher behind the site. A template is text with variables, such as {{ post.title }}; each part lists those it may use.
settings.search.separator.label: Separator
settings.search.description.label: Site description
settings.search.image.label: Default sharing image
settings.search.publisher.label: Publisher
settings.search.publisher.description: Who offers the site: every page's footer shows the publisher's name, organisation number, postal address, email and VAT number, and the structured data and the privacy texts name the publisher too. Sweden's e-handelslagen asks a business that offers services on its site to give its name, postal address, email and organisation number, its VAT number where it has one, the register it is entered in, and, under a permit or in a regulated profession, its supervisory authority. Everything filled in here is public, the organisation number too, which for a sole trader is the owner's personal identity number. Konzilo gives no legal advice: which details the site must give is the publisher's to decide.
settings.search.publisher.kind.label: Kind
settings.search.publisher.name.label: Name
settings.search.publisher.vatNumber.help: The VAT registration number, such as SE556677889901, where the publisher is registered for VAT.
The register the publisher is entered in, such as Bolagsverket's trade register, with the registration number where it differs from the organisation number.
settings.search.publisher.supervisoryAut: Only for a business that needs a permit, or that works in a regulated profession: the authority that supervises it, with its contact details, or the professional body it belongs to, with its professional title and the country that gave it.

settings.metaLine.label: Meta line
settings.metaLine.description: The line between a post's standfirst and its body that shows who wrote it, when and under which category, written by its type's format, the same for every post of the type. A format is text with variables in braces: {authors}, the authors' names with a comma between, and {category}, the category's name, for an article; {date}, the day the post was published, and {modified}, the day it last changed, where that is a later day, for a type whose posts have them. A variable without a value drops out with the words before it, back to the variable or the punctuation mark before them. A type without a format shows no meta line.
settings.metaLine.types.format.label: Format
settings.metaLine.types.format.help: Such as Published on {date} in {category} by {authors}. A field left empty is the type's default format, and a type without one shows no meta line.
settings.breadcrumbs.label: Breadcrumbs
settings.breadcrumbs.description: Whether a page's breadcrumbs end with the page itself, by type. The structured data always holds the page itself; a page right under the start page has no breadcrumbs without it.
settings.breadcrumbs.types.current.label: The page itself last
settings.breadcrumbs.types.current.help: Off, the breadcrumbs end at the level above the page.
settings.ai.label: AI visibility
settings.ai.description: How AI agents find the site's pages and may use them: which pages they get in Markdown, at the page's address with .md, and which of those llms.txt lists and llms-full.txt holds in full, for the start page and by type; the paths left out of all three; and the content signals robots.txt gives.
settings.ai.excludedPaths.label: Excluded paths
settings.ai.excludedPaths.help: One regular expression per line, without delimiters or flags, matched against each page's path from the site's root: ^/pages/ leaves out every page whose path begins /pages/, and /cookies/ every page with /cookies/ in its path. Case does not matter, and letters beyond English match as they read. A page whose path matches is left out of its Markdown, llms.txt and llms-full.txt. A line that is not a regular expression is not saved: the paths stay as they were, and the page says which line.
settings.ai.home.label: Start page
settings.ai.home.markdown.label: Markdown (.md)
settings.ai.home.llms.label: In llms.txt
settings.ai.home.llmsFull.label: In llms-full.txt
settings.ai.signals.label: Content signals
settings.ai.signals.search.label: Search
settings.ai.signals.search.help: Whether search engines may show the site's pages in their results: grant writes search=yes, reserve search=no, and defer says nothing, which leaves it to the site's other signals. Warning: reserve may take the site out of search results, and search engines may ignore it; to keep a page out of them, turn on Keep out of search engines under Search in its form instead. Note: grant may contradict a page hidden from search engines, which wins.
settings.ai.signals.aiInput.label: AI input
settings.ai.signals.aiInput.help: Whether AI may use the site's content to answer questions, which is what AI visibility is for: grant writes ai-input=yes, reserve ai-input=no, and defer says nothing. Note: reserve works against the rest of these settings.
settings.ai.signals.aiTrain.label: AI training
settings.ai.signals.aiTrain.help: Whether AI may be trained on the site's content: grant writes ai-train=yes and reserve ai-train=no; defer says nothing, which leaves it to law and practice, in many places a tacit yes.
settings.ai.types.markdown.label: Markdown (.md)
settings.ai.types.markdown.help: A Markdown version of each page, at its address with .md, made from the page as visitors see it.
settings.ai.types.llms.label: In llms.txt
settings.ai.types.llms.help: Each page listed in llms.txt, the site's index for AI agents, which links to its Markdown. Needs Markdown, and is off wherever Markdown is off.
settings.ai.types.llmsFull.label: In llms-full.txt
settings.ai.types.llmsFull.help: Each page's Markdown in llms-full.txt, the chosen pages in one document. Needs Markdown, and is off wherever Markdown is off.
settings.consent.label: Consent texts
settings.consent.description: What the privacy banner, the privacy settings, the content waiting for consent and the right to object to counting without storage say to visitors. A text left empty is the default in the site's language; {service} stands for a service's name.
settings.consent.bannerTitle.label: Banner: title
settings.consent.bannerText.label: Banner: text
settings.consent.bannerAccept.label: Banner: accept button
settings.consent.bannerReject.label: Banner: reject button

settings.consent.dialogReject.label: Privacy settings: reject button

settings.consent.dialogClose.label: Privacy settings: close button

settings.consent.footerWithdraw.label: Footer: withdraw consent
settings.consent.noticeWithdrawn.label: Notice: consent withdrawn
settings.consent.placeholderButton.label: Content waiting for consent: button
settings.consent.objectionText.label: Right to object: explanation
settings.consent.objectionText.help: The words in square brackets are the link that objects, such as [object]; without brackets the link follows the text.
settings.consent.objectionObjected.label: Right to object: once the visitor objects
settings.consent.objectionObjected.help: Shown once the visitor objects. The words in square brackets are the link that takes the objection back; without brackets the link follows the text.
settings.consent.objectionTitle.label: Right to object: confirmation's title
settings.consent.objectionAppeal.label: Right to object: confirmation
settings.consent.objectionConfirm.label: Right to object: confirm button
settings.consent.objectionCancel.label: Right to object: cancel button
settings.consent.necessaryName.label: Necessary: name
settings.consent.functionalName.label: Functional: name
settings.consent.statisticsName.label: Statistics: name
settings.consent.statisticsWithoutStorag: Statistics: description where visits are counted without storage before consent
settings.consent.marketingName.label: Marketing: name
settings.tagManager.label: Tag manager
settings.tagManager.description: What the public site loads to measure visits: Matomo Tag Manager, from the container set up in it, with its tags, or Matomo's own tracker, by the site's ID in Matomo, with no container. Either loads on the customer's domain alone, never at the pre-launch address, in a preview or locally, and only once the visitor consents to statistics, unless the site description departs from that. A container's tags fire on the visitor's consent, which the site gives the tag manager on every page and at every change; a tag that loads another service needs that service declared on the Services screen. Matomo itself, and how long it keeps what it measures, are set up in Matomo.
settings.tagManager.manager.label: Tag manager
settings.tagManager.manager.help: Matomo Tag Manager loads a container and the tags set up in it. Matomo loads Matomo's own tracker, which counts each page view, with no container.
settings.tagManager.address.label: Matomo address
settings.tagManager.address.help: The address of the Matomo instance, as the address bar shows it without index.php: https:// and its host, with a path where Matomo is below one, such as https://matomo.example.com/ or https://www.example.com/matomo/.
settings.tagManager.container.label: Container ID
settings.tagManager.container.help: For Matomo Tag Manager: the container's ID, eight letters and digits, as Matomo shows it under Tag Manager › Containers and in the code it offers to install: aBcD1234 in container_aBcD1234.js.
settings.tagManager.site.label: Site ID
settings.tagManager.site.help: For Matomo: the site's ID in Matomo, a whole number, as Matomo shows it under Websites › Manage and in the tracking code it offers: 3 in setSiteId('3').
settings.tagManager.cookieDomain.label: Cookie domain
settings.tagManager.cookieDomain.help: For Matomo, and only where the owner's sites below one domain are counted as one: that domain, such as example.com, which the site's own host is at or below. Matomo then keeps its cookies there, so a visitor who moves between the sites is one visitor. Leave it empty to keep them on the site's own host.
settings.tagManager.timeZone.label: Time zone
settings.tagManager.timeZone.help: For Matomo, where the site counts visits without storage before consent: the time zone the site has in Matomo, under Websites › Manage, by its name, such as Europe/Paris. Until a visitor allows statistics, the time of day of each visit is sent in it, since the visitor's own would read the time zone of their device. Leave it empty for UTC.
settings.tagManager.provider.label: Who runs Matomo
settings.tagManager.provider.description: Who runs the Matomo instance, which the privacy settings and the cookie declaration name as Matomo's provider. Leave all three empty when the site's publisher runs it; they then name the site itself. Where it is established outside the EU and EEA, they also say that what visitors' browsers send Matomo goes to its country.
settings.tagManager.provider.name.label: Legal name
settings.tagManager.provider.country.hel: The country it is established in, by its two-letter code, such as SE for Sweden.
settings.legalPages.label: Legal pages
settings.legalPages.description: The pages every page of the site links to from its footer.
settings.legalPages.privacyPolicy.label: Privacy policy
settings.legalPages.cookiePolicy.label: Cookie policy
settings.forms.label: Forms
settings.forms.description: Who gets each form's submissions by mail, what visitors see once they have sent it, and how many days the site keeps each submission. The recipients and the retention stay out of the published files; a submission held as spam is deleted after 7 days.
settings.forms.recipients.label: Recipients
settings.forms.confirmation.label: Confirmation text
settings.forms.retention.label: Retention in days
settings.notFound.label: Addresses not found
settings.notFound.description: The page visitors see at an address the site has nothing at, and where a redirect rule answers 404 or 410. The chosen page has no address of its own, and no list, menu or sitemap holds it; without one, the site shows a short text of its own.
settings.notFound.page.label: Page for addresses not found
settings.feeds.label: Feeds
settings.feeds.description: The site's RSS feeds, which feed readers and newsletter tools follow, at the addresses the site description gives them: one for each post type that declares one, and one for each term of a taxonomy that does. Each item begins with the post's featured image.
settings.feeds.item.label: Each item holds
settings.feeds.item.help: The summary is the post's excerpt, or else the start of its text. The whole text gives a feed reader the post's whole body too, as the site shows it.
settings.feeds.posts.label: Posts in each feed
settings.related.label: Related posts
settings.related.description: How “Recommended reading” under a post, and a post list ordered as related, rank the posts that share its terms: an article scores a point for each topic it shares and half a point for the same category, a post of another type a point for each term it shares, and each score is multiplied by its post's freshness, so that newer posts rank higher. A post that scores nothing is never shown.
settings.related.freshness.label: Freshness
settings.related.freshness.help: On, a post's score halves with each half-life of its age. Off, the score alone decides, and the newer post where two score the same.
settings.related.halfLife.label: Half-life in days
settings.related.halfLife.help: The days in which a post's freshness halves: at 90, a post 90 days old counts half as much as a new one, and one 180 days old a quarter. A shorter half-life favours newer posts more.

form.slugHint: The last part of the address. Made from the title if left empty.
form.name: Name
form.seoFollows: Left empty, the template for this type of post decides.
form.seoCanonicalHint: Where the original is, if this text was published elsewhere first: search engines then credit the original, and the sitemap leaves this post out. Left empty, the post's own address is canonical.
form.seoCanonicalPattern: Write a whole web address, starting with https:// or http://, such as https://www.example.com/the-original/.
form.breadcrumbHint: Instead of the title, when a shorter name fits better. The levels themselves follow from where the post sits.
form.headline: Main headline
form.workingNameHint: Shown in the lists of posts. The breadcrumb, and the slug of a new post, are made from it.
form.caption: Caption
form.libraryHint: Copied into a post when the image is chosen there, where it can then be changed for that use.
form.label: Label
form.labelHint: The post's title, if left empty.
form.otherPathHint: The path from the site's root, starting with /, such as /old-page/. Not a whole web address: the site can only answer at addresses of its own.
form.otherPathPattern: Write a path starting with /, such as /old-page/, not a whole web address.
form.urlHint: Only for an entry that does not lead to a post.
form.author: Author
refusal.element-not-taken: this kind of post cannot hold {element}; take it out, or ask the site's developer to allow it
refusal.inline-element: the site cannot publish {inline} in {element}; take it out

warning.departure-tracker: the departure counts without storage only with Matomo's own tracker, which the site settings do not choose, so nothing counts before consent
warning.schema-not-offered: {plural} cannot have "{value}" as their structured data type, so it is left out and their default applies; choose one of {types}
warning.scheduled-passed: the post is scheduled for {moment}, which had already passed when the site first read it, so it is published at once, with that moment as its date
about.directive-leaf: ::{name}, on a line of its own
about.kind-boolean: yes or no, true or false
about.svg-doctype: a document type with declarations of its own
about.svg-stylesheet: a stylesheet from outside the file
about.svg-animation: an animation that sets a reference or a handler
about.svg-proportions: no proportions: give it a viewBox, or a width and a height
about.target-browser: "{target}" is not an address as a browser sends it
about.target-site: "{target}" is not an address of a site
about.target-form: "{target}" is neither an address on the site, starting with a slash, nor an https:// address
about.target-group-none: its target holds {reference}, but the pattern has no group
about.target-group-one: its target holds {reference}, but the pattern has one group, $1
about.target-groups: its target holds {reference}, but the pattern has {groups} groups, $1 to {last}
about.target-group-host: its target holds a group in the host of its address, which only its path may
about.target-loop: it matches its own target again, as {path}, so it would loop
failure.not-read: the source could not be read, so visitors still see the last version
failure.check-broke: the check of what was saved broke, so visitors still see the last version
failure.not-built: the site could not be built from it, so visitors still see the last version
failure.not-released: the new version of the site could not be put in place, so visitors still see the last version
failure.stopped: the build would take most of the site's posts off it, so it waits until the deletion is confirmed
